# Enterprise GitHub apps

Two optional, platform-level GitHub Apps let admin automate work that otherwise needs a human on GitHub: installing an agent's App on an enterprise-owned org (the **installer** App), and, in a later phase, reconciling repository access (the **lookup** App). This page covers what each App is for, the exact permissions, setup, why there is no shared published App, the admin isolation exception, and how keys are stored. Per-agent App auth is a different thing and is covered in [`github-multi-org.md`](./github-multi-org.md). File map: [`agent-key-files.md`](./agent-key-files.md).

The feature is **optional and per deployment**. With no rows configured it is off and nothing else changes; agents keep installing their Apps by hand as described in [`github-multi-org.md`](./github-multi-org.md).

## The two Apps

| Role | Used for | Installed on |
|------|----------|--------------|
| `installer` | Installing an agent's App on an enterprise-owned org (`POST /github-enterprise/orgs/{org}/install`) and listing the orgs it can install on. | The **enterprise** (not an org). |
| `lookup` | Read-only lookups, such as collaborator permission, used by later repository reconciliation. It has no install route. | **Every org**, with **all repositories**. |

At most one App per role is stored, so a deployment has at most two.

## Required permissions

Permissions were verified against GitHub's REST API description and the "permissions required for GitHub Apps" docs while building `GithubEnterpriseClient` (GHE-1.2); the verification notes are in the header of `admin/src/github-enterprise-client.ts`.

| App | Permission | Level | Why |
|-----|------------|-------|-----|
| Installer | Enterprise: `enterprise_organization_installations` | **Read and write** (read covers the list calls only) | Read for listing installable orgs and an org's installations; write for installing (and removing) an App on an org. Required: validation fails without it. |
| Installer | Enterprise: `enterprise_organization_installation_repositories` | **Read and write** (read covers list only) | Read for listing repositories an installation can access; write for granting and revoking repository access (repository management). The settings page asks for it; validation only warns when it is missing. |
| Lookup | Repository: `metadata` | **read** | Collaborator-permission lookups are listed under Metadata read, not Administration. Required: validation fails without it. |
| Lookup | Organization: `members` | **read** | Lets the lookup see organization membership. Optional: validation only warns when it is missing. |

Notes:

- The enterprise endpoints exist only on GitHub Enterprise Cloud, and "can only be called by a GitHub App installed on the enterprise that owns the organization". The installer App must therefore be installed on the enterprise itself.
- Validation fails only for the required permissions: installer needs `enterprise_organization_installations` at `write`; lookup needs `metadata` at `read` or `write`.
- The two optional permissions above produce non-failing warnings (see Setup step 4).
- `GithubEnterpriseClient` implements repository access management (list, add, remove, and all/selected toggle); these operations require `enterprise_organization_installation_repositories` at write.
- **Unverified:** whether Metadata read alone suffices for the collaborator-permission lookup at runtime has not been verified live. This stays flagged until GHE-2.7 checks it.

## Setup

Admin only. Credentials are pasted; admin does not create these Apps for you.

The settings page shows these same steps on each card, and notes that a GitHub Enterprise Cloud enterprise is required. On each App, ignore the callback URL, request user authorization, expire user authorization tokens and device flow options, and uncheck webhook Active.

1. **Create the installer App** in GitHub under your enterprise's Settings, GitHub Apps, New GitHub App (an enterprise-owned App). Under Enterprise permissions grant both `enterprise_organization_installations` and `enterprise_organization_installation_repositories` at Read and write. Install it on the enterprise. Generate a private key.
2. **Create the lookup App** under your organization's Settings, Developer settings, GitHub Apps, New GitHub App. Grant Repository `Metadata` at Read and Organization `Members` at Read. Install it on every org, choosing **all repositories** (not selected repositories only). Generate a private key.
3. Open `/admin/settings/github-enterprise` (admin-only; **Settings** in the nav). On each card enter the App id (on the App's settings page), the App slug (the last part of `github.com/apps/<slug>`) and the private key, pasted as PEM or uploaded as a `.pem` file. The installer card also takes the **enterprise slug** (the last part of `github.com/enterprises/<slug>`).
4. Use **Validate** on each card. Validation authenticates as the App, checks the required permission and records the result and time on the card. A failure shows a generic reason, except that a 404 on the installer's `GET /enterprises/{slug}/installation` lookup reports that the App is not installed on that enterprise or the slug is wrong. Missing optional permissions appear as non-failing warnings on the card and in the validate response (`warnings`): the installer without `enterprise_organization_installation_repositories` (write) and the lookup without Organization Members (read). Warnings never change a valid result to invalid. Keys are never echoed.
5. To install an agent's App on an org, use the org list on the same page. Install resolves the App's `client_id` (the install call needs it, not the numeric id) in this order:
   - the agent's stored `GH_APP_CLIENT_ID`, when set and well-formed. This is the only route for a **private** App.
   - otherwise the agent's `GH_APP_SLUG`, resolved through the public `GET /apps/{slug}`. This needs the App to be public.

   An agent with neither is refused with a 422, as is a private App with no stored client id (the message says to store its `GH_APP_CLIENT_ID`). The org list shows the same reason up front when an agent is selected.
6. **The agent's installations card stays empty until the agent has `GH_APP_ID` and a private key.** Installing an App on an org does not populate the card: it shows what the agent runtime reports from its own credentials ([`github-multi-org.md`](./github-multi-org.md)), and admin never calls GitHub on the agent's behalf for it. Until those are set the runtime reports nothing.

The same operations are available over the API: `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /github-enterprise/apps[/{role}]`, `POST /github-enterprise/apps/{role}/validate`, `GET /github-enterprise/orgs`, `POST /github-enterprise/orgs/{org}/install` (see [`admin-service.md`](./admin-service.md)).

## Repository reconcile

Reconcile keeps an agent's repo scope within what its bound GitHub user can actually push to. It is the enforcer of that rule: session members can still edit an agent's `repos` (see [The member-edit caveat](#the-member-edit-caveat)), so reconcile is what brings the scope back in line. It needs the agent's `githubUsername`, both enterprise Apps, and a `GH_APP_ID` in the agent's own stored env (the numeric id of that agent's GitHub App, whose installations are changed).

### Plan, then apply

Two platform-admin-only routes (session members, ops keys and agent keys get `403`). These routes remain available for API consumers, though the admin UI's detail-page card that used them has been replaced by direct Installation Repos management (IRM-1.4):

- `POST /agents/{id}/github-reconcile/plan` is read-only. The optional body `{addRepos: ["owner/repo"]}` names repos to add. It returns `status: planned` with `planHash`, `empty`, the `diff` (`installationAdds`, `installationRemoves`, `configAdds`, `configRemoves`), `skippedOrgs`, `rejectedAdds`, `warnings` and `affectedOpenWork` (the open work the removals would touch). Unknown agent is `404`.
- `POST /agents/{id}/github-reconcile/apply` takes `{planHash, addRepos?, confirmRemovals?}`. It **re-plans server-side** and applies only when the fresh plan hashes to the `planHash` the admin reviewed, so what is applied is what was reviewed. Pass the same `addRepos` used for the plan.

### Direct installation repo management

Without a plan step, a platform admin can manage the repos on the agent's own App installation (the App named by its stored `GH_APP_ID`). Same auth as reconcile: session members, ops keys and agent keys get `403`.

- `GET /agents/{id}/github-installation/repos` lists, per org the agent App is installed on, the installation's repos. With a bound `githubUsername`, each repo carries `userCanPush` from the access lookup, but only when that org's lookup result is complete; otherwise the field is omitted (never `false`).
- `POST /agents/{id}/github-installation/repos` and `POST /agents/{id}/github-installation/repos/remove` take `{repos: ["owner/repo"]}` and add or remove those repos on the installation. The agent's configured `repos` are not changed.

Errors: unknown agent `404`; no `GH_APP_ID` `422`; the App not installed on a repo's org `409` (nothing is changed or audited); GitHub refusing the change `502`. Every add or remove writes one `GitHubReconcileAudit` row (`planHash` is `direct:add` or `direct:remove`, `caller` is the key or session name, the repos are in `diff.installationAdds` or `installationRemoves`); a GitHub failure writes a `failed` row with only the repos that landed.

Apply checks run in this order, and the first that matches decides the outcome:

| Outcome | HTTP | When |
|---------|------|------|
| `skipped` | 200 | No GitHub username bound, or the Apps are not configured. Nothing changes and no audit row is written. |
| `noop` | 200 | The fresh plan is empty. This is what makes a second apply idempotent. |
| stale plan | 409 | The fresh plan's hash differs from `planHash`. Re-plan and review again. |
| removal cap | 422 | More than 10 repos would be removed and `confirmRemovals` is not `true`. |
| `applied` / `failed` | 200 | Applied, or an installation or config step threw. Both carry `auditId`, `planHash` and `diff`; `failed` also carries `error`. |

Order of effects on apply: installation adds, installation removes, the agent's `repos`, the audit row, then blocking open work.

### The rules

- **Removals only, adds only when named.** The desired scope is the agent's current repos minus those the bound user cannot push to. Newly accessible repos are never added on their own. A repo is added only when the admin names it in `addRepos`, the user can push to it, and its basename does not collide with a repo already kept (clones are keyed by basename). Anything else lands in `rejectedAdds` with a reason.
- **Unknown is never none.** Removals are skipped for an org whose access listing is missing, `partial` or failed, and for an org whose lookup App is installed on selected repositories only. Each is reported in `skippedOrgs` and as a warning. If the user is unbound, not found on GitHub or could not be verified, the whole plan is `skipped`.
- **Subset invariant.** The agent's repos stay a subset of the agent App's installation repos. A removed repo also leaves the installation, a named add is installed first when absent, and a configured repo that the installation does not cover is dropped with a warning.
- **Removal cap.** Applying more than 10 removals needs `confirmRemovals: true`. The cap guards against a bad lookup (for example a revoked or mis-scoped lookup App) silently stripping most of an agent's scope in one click.
- **Inert when unbound or unconfigured.** With no bound username, or with the enterprise Apps not configured, plan and apply return `skipped` and make no installation calls. An agent with no (or a non-numeric) `GH_APP_ID` in its stored env reports `skipped` with a reason naming `GH_APP_ID`; an org where the agent's App is not installed fails the plan with an error naming that org.
- **Idempotent.** Planning over an already-reconciled state gives an empty diff and the same hash; applying it is a `noop`.

### Audit entry

Every apply attempt that gets past the skip and no-op checks, successful or failed, writes one `GitHubReconcileAudit` row: `agentId`, `caller` (the API key name), `planHash`, `diff`, `result` (`{status: "applied"}` or `{status: "failed", error}`) and `createdAt`, indexed on `(agentId, createdAt)`. Stale-plan and removal-cap refusals write nothing, and neither do skipped or no-op applies.

### Open work

A host can supply an optional `OpenWorkPort` through the admin extension's `services.openWork`. Plan lists the open work on repos the plan removes (`affectedOpenWork`); apply then blocks it with the reason `repo removed from agent by GitHub reconcile (<repo>)`. Blocking happens after the audit write and a port failure is a warning on an otherwise `applied` result, never a failed apply. With no port, nothing is listed or blocked.

### Removing repos the bound user lost access to

A platform admin can remove, from both the agent App's installation and the agent's `repos`, every repo the bound `githubUsername` can no longer push to. It never adds repos, and there is no plan hash: the admin confirms an explicit list and the server re-checks it. Same auth as reconcile (session members, ops keys and agent keys get `403`).

- `GET /agents/{id}/github-lost-access/preview` is read-only (nothing changed or audited). It returns `repos` (with `installationRemoves` and `configRemoves`), `skippedOrgs`, `warnings` and `openWork`: the agent's open tasks and PRs on those repos that the removal would block (empty with no open-work port; a port failure is a warning).
- `POST /agents/{id}/github-lost-access/remove` takes `{repos: ["owner/repo"], confirmRemovals?}`. Each named repo is re-checked against the user's current access; only those still without push access are removed. Named repos left alone (the user can still push, the org is skipped, or the repo is on neither side) are reported in `notRemoved`.

The reconcile safety rules apply: orgs whose listing is missing, `partial` or failed, or whose lookup App is installed on selected repositories only, are skipped and reported; an unbound, not-found or unverified user (or no `GH_APP_ID`, or unconfigured Apps) makes the whole call `skipped` with nothing changed and no audit row; more than 10 removals without `confirmRemovals: true` is `422`. `noop` when nothing named still lacks access. Order of effects: installation removals, the agent's `repos`, one `GitHubReconcileAudit` row (`planHash` `lost-access:remove`), then the agent's open work on the removed repos is blocked through the `OpenWorkPort` with a reason naming the repo and that the bound user lost push access (a port failure is a warning, not a failed call). GitHub refusing a removal is `502`, with a `failed` audit row recording only what landed.

### The member-edit caveat

Reconcile is not a live guard. Session members can still change an agent's `repos` through `PATCH /agents/{id}` and the repo add routes, and nothing rechecks the bound user's access at that moment. A repo the user cannot push to can therefore sit in the scope until an admin plans and applies a reconcile. Run it after membership or access changes, and treat it as the enforcer rather than the validator.

## Why there is no shared published App

A published App that every deployment used would need one private key shared across all of them. That key could mint installation tokens for **every customer's installations**, so leaking it from any one deployment would compromise all of them. Instead each deployment creates and owns its own installer and lookup pair, and the blast radius of a key is one deployment.

## The admin isolation exception

Admin normally never calls GitHub with App credentials: per-agent App keys live in the agent's env and are used by the agent runtime, and admin only displays what agents report ([`github-multi-org.md`](./github-multi-org.md#admin-status-card)).

The enterprise client is the **one exception**. `GithubEnterpriseClient` and the `/github-enterprise` routes sign App JWTs inside admin. To keep that exception contained:

- The keys live in their own `GitHubEnterpriseApp` table, deliberately **not** in `AgentEnv`, and are stored apart from agent credentials.
- Keys never reach agents: not the config bundle, not agent-bearer routes, not env serialization. `github-enterprise-isolation.unit.test.ts` pins this.
- Read paths return metadata and a `keySet` flag, never the key; the settings page never renders it; error messages never include the PEM.
- The routes are admin-only.

## Encryption

Private keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they are stored, using `SHIPWRIGHT_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. Unlike agent env values, which fall back to plain text when the key is unset, this feature is strict:

- Saving **refuses** (422) when `SHIPWRIGHT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is not configured. There is no plain-text fallback.
- A key that cannot be decrypted is an error; ciphertext is never passed on as a PEM.
- There is **no key rotation**. Changing `SHIPWRIGHT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` makes stored keys undecryptable; delete and re-paste each App's key afterwards.
